source.section: Form IL-1040 PDF page 1, Lines 1-19; Instructions PDF page 8, Lines 10-12; rate Instructions PDF page 1; Line 10a chart and Income Exceptions, Instructions PDF page 8

worked: Federal AGI = wages (person 0) 247,850.00 + IRA distribution (person 0) 2,150.00 = 250,000.00. Federal taxable income = 250,000.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 = 234,250.00 (federal senior deduction ignored; federal figures are given, not tested; Illinois starts from federal AGI). Form IL-1040 Line 1 federal AGI 250,000.00. Line 2 federally tax-exempt interest 0.00. Line 3 other additions 0.00. Line 4 = 250,000.00. Line 5 IRA distribution 2,150.00 = 2,150.00. Lines 6 and 7 0.00. Line 8 = 2,150.00. Line 9 base income = 250,000.00 - 2,150.00 = 247,850.00. Income Exceptions: federal AGI 250,000.00 is not greater than 250,000.00, so the allowance stands. Line 10a 2,850.00. Line 10b 0.00. Lines 10c and 10d 0.00. Line 10 = 2,850.00. Line 11 net income = 247,850.00 - 2,850.00 = 245,000.00. Line 12 tax = 245,000.00 x 4.95% = 12,127.5000. The form takes whole dollars only and would show 12,128.00; expected uses the formula to the cent. Lines 13-18 0.00 (no credits in the projection). Line 19 state income tax = 12,127.50. The printed word is 'greater than', so federal AGI of exactly 250,000.00 keeps the allowance.
